lessons.title: DNA Analysis in Forensic Science and Paternity Testing — RFLPs and Fingerprinting
lessons.notes_html:
Identifying a person from DNA

DNA analysis identifies a person from a very small sample such as blood, hair, semen or skin cells, because the pattern of DNA markers of every person (except identical twins) is unique.

DNA analysis in forensic science

In forensic science, DNA fingerprinting of evidence from a crime scene is matched with the DNA of suspects to identify the criminal or to prove an innocent person free.

DNA analysis in paternity testing

In paternity testing the markers of a child are compared with those of the mother and the alleged father, since half of the child's markers must come from the father.

Methods used in DNA analysis

  • Extraction: extraction of DNA.
  • Amplification: amplification of DNA by PCR.
  • Cutting: cutting with restriction enzymes to obtain RFLPs.
  • Separation: separation by gel electrophoresis.
  • Comparison: comparison of STR (short tandem repeat) patterns.

Chain: extraction of DNA → amplification by PCR → cutting with restriction enzymes to obtain RFLPs → separation by gel electrophoresis → comparison of STR patterns.

RFLPs — restriction fragment length polymorphisms

RFLPs are differences in the lengths of DNA fragments produced when DNA of different individuals is cut with the same restriction enzyme. These differences arise because mutations change the cutting sites of the enzyme from person to person.

  • Genetic markers: RFLP patterns are used as genetic markers.
  • Uses: RFLP patterns are used in DNA fingerprinting, disease diagnosis and mapping of genes.

lessons.title: Role of Microorganisms in Human Welfare
lessons.notes_html:
Microbes in human welfare

Microbes are used in food processing and in sewage treatment. In both fields microbes convert waste or raw material into useful, safe products.

Microbes in food processing

Microbes are used to make many everyday foods, improving their taste, texture and keeping quality.

  • Lactobacillus: converts milk into curd and yoghurt.
  • Saccharomyces cerevisiae: the yeast used to raise bread dough and to produce alcohol.
  • Other microbes: used in cheese, vinegar and fermented foods.

Yeast and the puffy appearance of dough

The yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae ferments sugars in the dough and releases carbon dioxide gas. The trapped gas bubbles make the dough rise and give it a puffy, spongy appearance, which is used in making bread.

  • Fermentation: yeast ferments sugars in the dough.
  • Carbon dioxide: gas released during fermentation is trapped as bubbles in the dough.
  • Result: the dough rises and becomes puffy and spongy.

Microbes in sewage treatment

In sewage treatment, microbes do the main cleaning work. Aerobic bacteria and other microorganisms in secondary treatment decompose the organic pollutants of sewage into harmless substances, and anaerobic bacteria digest the sludge, producing methane gas that can be used as fuel.

Steps of sewage treatment

Sewage treatment is done in three main steps: primary, secondary and tertiary treatment.

  • Primary treatment: the physical first stage, in which sewage is passed through screens and sedimentation tanks and floating and suspended solids are removed by screening, filtration and sedimentation. The settled solid material forms sludge, the clear liquid is called effluent, and the liquid passes on for biological treatment.
  • Secondary treatment: a biological process in which air is bubbled through the effluent and aerobic microbes decompose the dissolved organic matter, greatly reducing its harmful content. The microbes then settle as activated sludge, part of which is used again and part sent for sludge digestion.
  • Tertiary treatment: the water is further purified by chemical methods and disinfection, for example with chlorine or ultraviolet light, to remove remaining nutrients, pathogens and chemicals before the water is released or reused.
StageType of processMain work
Primary treatmentPhysicalFloating and suspended solids removed by screening, filtration and sedimentation; settled solids form sludge, clear liquid is effluent
Secondary treatmentBiologicalAir bubbled through effluent; aerobic microbes decompose dissolved organic matter; microbes settle as activated sludge
Tertiary treatmentChemical and disinfectionRemaining nutrients, pathogens and chemicals removed, for example with chlorine or ultraviolet light, before release or reuse

Sludge digestion

Sludge digestion is a biological process in which organic solids are decomposed into stable substances. During sludge digestion, anaerobic microbes break down the organic matter of sludge into stable, harmless substances, along with gases such as methane. Part of the activated sludge is sent for sludge digestion by anaerobic bacteria, which also produce biogas. The digested sludge can then be dried and safely used as manure.

  • Anaerobic microbes: break down the organic matter of sludge.
  • Stable substances: the harmless end products of digestion.
  • Methane / biogas: gas produced during digestion, which can be used as fuel.
  • Digested sludge: can be dried and safely used as manure.

lessons.title: Food Production — Livestock, Milk Breeds and Vegetables
lessons.notes_html:
Food production from livestock

Livestock and dairy animals are a major part of food production. They provide highly nutritious food and many other products for human welfare.

Role of livestock

Livestock animals such as cow, buffalo, goat, sheep and poultry provide highly nutritious food in the form of milk, meat and eggs, which supply proteins, fats and vitamins.

  • Food: milk, meat and eggs, supplying proteins, fats and vitamins.
  • Other products: wool, leather and other products.
  • Draught power: power for farming and transport.
  • Manure: manure for fields.
  • Income and employment: livestock is a major source of income and employment for rural families and an important part of the national economy.

Top milk producing animal of Pakistan

The Nili-Ravi buffalo, a famous breed of Punjab, is the top milk producing animal of Pakistan. A good animal gives a high daily yield of milk with high fat content, so it is most valued by dairy farmers.

  • Nili-Ravi: buffalo breed of Punjab; top milk producing animal of Pakistan, with high daily yield and high fat content.

Outstanding milk producing breeds of cow

Outstanding milk producing breeds of cow include local breeds and exotic high-yielding breeds, and crosses of the two.

  • Sahiwal: a local breed, well adapted to the hot climate of Pakistan and giving good yields.
  • Red Sindhi: a local breed, well adapted to the hot climate of Pakistan and giving good yields.
  • Holstein Friesian: an exotic breed and the highest milk producer.
  • Jersey: an exotic breed kept for rich, high-fat milk.
  • Brown Swiss: an exotic breed kept for rich, high-fat milk.
  • Crosses: crosses of local breeds with exotic breeds combine high yield with adaptation to local conditions.

Winter and summer vegetables

French beans and cauliflower grow best in cool weather, so in Pakistan they are sown and harvested as winter vegetables. High summer heat spoils their growth and, in cauliflower, prevents proper curd formation.

  • Winter vegetables: French beans and cauliflower, growing best in cool weather.

lessons.title: Disease Control — Vaccination, Vaccines and Integrated Management
lessons.notes_html:
Vaccination and protection against infectious disease

Vaccination introduces a weakened or killed pathogen, or its toxin, into the body, so the immune system makes antibodies and memory cells against it without causing the disease. When the real pathogen later attacks, the body responds quickly and the person does not become ill.

What vaccination is

Vaccination is the process of introducing a vaccine, made from weakened or killed microbes or their inactivated toxins, into the body to protect it against a specific disease. The method was first developed by Edward Jenner in 1796 using cowpox against smallpox. The vaccine acts as an antigen: the body produces antibodies and memory cells, so on later natural infection the immune response is rapid and strong and the disease is prevented.

  • Vaccine: made from weakened or killed microbes or their inactivated toxins.
  • Antigen action: the vaccine acts as an antigen and stimulates antibody and memory cell formation.
  • Later infection: the immune response is rapid and strong, and the disease is prevented.
  • Edward Jenner: first developed vaccination in 1796, using cowpox against smallpox.

Importance of vaccination

Vaccination of a whole population has controlled or eradicated dangerous infectious diseases such as smallpox and polio. Vaccination has eradicated smallpox, has nearly eradicated polio, and controls diseases such as measles, diphtheria, tetanus, hepatitis and COVID-19, saving millions of lives, especially of children, and reducing the cost of treatment.

  • Eradicated: smallpox.
  • Nearly eradicated: polio.
  • Controlled: measles, diphtheria, tetanus, hepatitis and COVID-19.
  • Benefit: millions of lives saved, especially of children, and reduced cost of treatment.

DT vaccine and diphtheria

DT vaccine contains diphtheria (and tetanus) toxoid, that is the inactivated toxin of the bacteria. It stimulates the body to make antibodies that protect against diphtheria.

  • DT vaccine: contains diphtheria and tetanus toxoid.
  • Toxoid: the inactivated toxin of the bacteria.
  • Protection: stimulates the body to make antibodies against diphtheria.

Tetanus and Clostridium tetani

Clostridium tetani, which causes tetanus, is a bacterium. It is a rod-shaped bacterium found in soil and dust that enters the body through wounds. Its toxin affects the nervous system and causes the painful muscle stiffness of tetanus.

  • Clostridium tetani: a rod-shaped bacterium, not a virus, parasite or fungus.
  • Habitat and entry: found in soil and dust; enters the body through wounds.
  • Toxin effect: affects the nervous system and causes painful muscle stiffness.

MMR vaccine

MMR is a combined vaccine whose name is made from the first letters of the three viral diseases it prevents: measles, mumps and rubella. It is given to children to provide immunity against all three diseases together.

VaccineProtects againstKey fact
DTDiphtheria (and tetanus)Contains diphtheria and tetanus toxoid, the inactivated bacterial toxin
MMRMeasles, mumps and rubellaCombined vaccine for three viral diseases, given to children

Integrated disease management

Integrated disease management means the planned control of the serious and common diseases of a population by using all suitable measures together, instead of depending on one method alone. Used together, these measures reduce the spread and severity of diseases effectively and economically.

  • Vaccination: one of the combined measures.
  • Healthy habits and sanitation: part of the combined approach.
  • Clean water and food: part of the combined approach.
  • Early diagnosis and treatment: part of the combined approach.
  • Biological control: control using other living organisms.

lessons.title: Breeding Methods and Genetic Engineering
lessons.notes_html:
Improving organisms for human welfare

Selection, hybridisation, back cross and genetic engineering are methods used to improve plants and animals and to enhance useful characteristics.

Back cross

When an F1 hybrid is crossed with either of its parents, the cross is called a back cross. Breeders use it to transfer a desired character of the hybrid into the parent variety while keeping most of the parent's good qualities.

  • Back cross: crossing of an F1 hybrid with either of its parents.
  • Purpose: to transfer a desired character of the hybrid into the parent variety while keeping most of the parent's good qualities.

Selection, back cross and hybridisation compared

Selection is the choosing of plants or animals with desired characters for breeding. Selection improves a breed by repeatedly breeding from the best existing individuals of the same variety, while hybridisation produces a new hybrid by crossing two different varieties or breeds to combine their desired characters.

MethodMeaning
SelectionChoosing plants or animals with desired characters for breeding; improves a breed by repeatedly breeding from the best existing individuals of the same variety

HybridisationProduces a new hybrid by crossing two different varieties or breeds to combine their desired characters

French beans and cauliflower also belong with the winter vegetables, as they grow best in cool weather.

Genetic engineering

Genetic engineering is the science that deals with the modification of DNA and enhances the characteristic of an organism. Genetic engineering directly changes the DNA of an organism by removing, altering or adding genes. In this way a desired characteristic is enhanced or a new useful characteristic is introduced into the organism.

  • Genetic engineering: direct change to the DNA of an organism by removing, altering or adding genes.
  • Result: a desired characteristic is enhanced, or a new useful characteristic is introduced.
